newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia may allow foreigners to own real estate.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia may allow foreigners to own real estate.

text.p: Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said on Tuesday he would meet parliamentary parties to seek support for a constitutional amendment to enable foreigners to own real estate in Slovenia.

"I will soon hold a meeting with all parliamentary parties where we will try to assess whether the change would be supported by a necessary two-third majority in parliament," Drnovsek told a news conference.
Sources close to the cabinet said Drnovsek was expected to meet all the parties in the first half of May.
Last year Slovenia agreed to change its constitution to allow foreigners to own real estate in the country within four years of an association agreement with the European Union taking effect.

The accord, which is a trade and co-operation pact that carries with it a promise of eventual EU membership, was signed in June 1996 and is expected to be ratified by Slovenia in May and enforced next year.
Drnovsek said earlier that the constitution would be amended as soon as it became clear that the change would be supported by a sufficient majority in parliament.
Slovenia is the only one of the successor states of the former Yugoslavia to have signed the EU association agreement.
